description: The runbooks gcp_runbooks.BigQueryRunbookStore seeds and retrieves via nearest() (bag-of-words cosine match against the Predict-stage event's query_text) to ground the Reason-stage LLM call. This is what the agent itself consults mid-incident -- separate from kb-incidents.json (postmortems on building/operating the system).

runbooks.title: Sustained blocked sessions
runbooks.body: active_blocked_sessions has stayed at or above the anomaly threshold for CONSECUTIVE_ANOMALY_THRESHOLD consecutive ticks. Identify the session currently holding the lock via v$session.blocking_session, then terminate exactly that session -- ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION 'sid,serial#' IMMEDIATE -- to release every session waiting behind it.

runbooks.title: Library cache contention
runbooks.match_key: library cache contention shared pool fragmentation high parse
runbooks.body: High hard-parse rates and library cache contention driven by shared pool fragmentation. Flush the shared pool -- ALTER SYSTEM FLUSH SHARED_POOL -- to clear fragmented and stale cursors and relieve contention. Auto-executes at Tier 2: allowed without human approval, but every run is logged loudly to the audit trail.

runbooks.title: AlloyDB blocking session
runbooks.match_key: blocking_session pg_locks lock_wait blocking backend pg_stat_activity
runbooks.body: A Postgres backend is confirmed holding a lock that is blocking other sessions, identified via pg_stat_activity / pg_locks (alloydb_find_blocking_session). Terminate exactly that backend -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) -- using the pid returned by the lookup, never a guessed value, to release everything waiting behind it.

runbooks.title: AlloyDB runaway query
runbooks.match_key: runaway_query long_running query_duration high cpu backend
runbooks.body: A single query has been running far longer than expected, consuming excessive CPU/IO on its backend. Terminate that backend directly -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) -- same underlying mechanism as alloydb_kill_blocking_session, kept as a separate allowlisted action so it is audited and reasoned about under its own name.

runbooks.title: AlloyDB idle-in-transaction buildup
runbooks.body: Backends have been sitting idle-in-transaction past a safe threshold (300s in the reference config), holding locks and connection slots for no active work. Batch-terminate every matching backend -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'idle in transaction' AND state_change < now() - interval '{idle_seconds} seconds'. Auto-executes at Tier 2: allowed without human approval, but every run is logged loudly to the audit trail -- can affect multiple sessions at once, broader blast radius than a Tier 1 single-backend kill.

runbooks.title: AlloyDB connection storm
runbooks.match_key: AlloyDB connection storm -- last-resort reset requested
runbooks.body: Last-resort, instance-wide reset: terminates every other active session on the database -- SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND datname = current_database(). Requires human approval via Slack before it ever runs (Tier 3) -- approving it during a live demo genuinely terminates every other session, so only approve this in a controlled setting.
